source.name: Chamath Palihapitiya — Ambitious but Inconsistent (Delete the Apps)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 34–36; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: A brief review can notice what is working alongside what needs attention, rather than seeing only deficits.
pivots.limits: Gratitude is optional and never cancels real problems or requires forced positivity.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Emotional Fluidity and Clean Fuel (Rich Roll)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 31–37; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: A feeling can be acknowledged without shame and without directing harmful behavior at another person.
pivots.limits: Feelings are not wrongdoing. Do not infer trauma, illness or responsibility for harm done to the person.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Emotional Fluidity and Clean Fuel (Rich Roll)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 45–47; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: Rather than arguing with self-criticism using another rigid rule, try a small different response and notice whether it helps.
pivots.limits: Experiments are optional, not treatment; stop if distress increases and seek suitable support.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Emotional Fluidity and Clean Fuel (Rich Roll)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 63–69; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: Look at a recurring pattern with curiosity without treating the whole person as defective or broken.
pivots.limits: Curiosity does not remove accountability or replace professional care.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Breaking the Helplessness Loop (Chris Williamson)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 31–35; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: Describe a boundary through your own choices and actions, rather than a demand to control another person’s response.
pivots.limits: No requirement for warmth, contact, reconciliation or remaining in danger.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Breaking the Helplessness Loop (Chris Williamson)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 41–43; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: If useful, explore a recurring thought through private writing or a brief pause without directing the emotion at someone else.
pivots.limits: Private expression is not a substitute for human sharing and is not a guaranteed cure; do not prolong reassurance loops.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Breaking the Helplessness Loop (Chris Williamson)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 55–57; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: A decision can leave room for feelings you cannot predict, instead of requiring a guarantee that you will feel a certain way.
pivots.limits: Use available facts and judgment. Willingness to feel discomfort is not consent to harm.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Dissolving Procrastination (Coaching Session)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 21–27; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: Notice whether pressure to guarantee a result is making it harder to start, then choose one manageable part of the task.
pivots.limits: This is one possible lens, not an explanation for every delay; practical barriers still matter.

source.name: Joe Hudson — Dissolving Procrastination (Coaching Session)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 29–33; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: Consider whether your self-management is as reasonable and respectful as what you would offer another person.
pivots.limits: Kindness can coexist with limits and accountability; no inference of laziness or wrongdoing.

source.name: Jim Rohn — The Speech That Will Change Your Life
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 49–55; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: Name a concrete kind of help you need and consider an appropriate person or resource to ask.
pivots.limits: Asking does not guarantee help and does not authorize disclosure or contact; the person decides.

source.name: Rick Rubin - Creativity, Taste and the Four Phases (The Diary of a CEO)

pivots.text: A chosen task can begin before reluctance disappears. Try a manageable start rather than demanding the perfect mood.
pivots.limits: Rest, illness and overload can make stopping appropriate. This is not a discipline test.

source.name: Rick Rubin - Creativity, Taste and the Four Phases (The Diary of a CEO)

pivots.text: Keep a plan revisable as experience changes, without needing to predict an entire future before acting.
pivots.limits: Do not replace practical commitments, financial planning or informed decisions with intuition.

source.name: Rick Rubin - Creativity, Taste and the Four Phases (The Diary of a CEO)

pivots.text: Define a reasonable completion criterion for work, then distinguish releasing it from controlling how it will be received.
pivots.limits: Keep real follow-up duties and contractual obligations; do not promise acceptance or success.

source.name: Rick Rubin - Creativity, Taste and the Four Phases (The Diary of a CEO)

pivots.text: Consider genuinely different viewpoints, then make a bounded decision without requiring perfect certainty.
pivots.limits: More research is not always better. Avoid endless checking and do not outsource judgment.

source.name: Rick Rubin - Creativity, Taste and the Four Phases (The Diary of a CEO)

pivots.text: Before optimizing for approval, clarify what you honestly want a creative piece to express.
pivots.limits: Artistic expression and solving a customer’s problem have different obligations; do not dismiss audience requirements.

source.name: Rick Rubin - Creativity, Taste and the Four Phases (The Diary of a CEO)

pivots.text: A fixed label about ability need not prevent a small, chosen experiment in learning a skill.
pivots.limits: Do not deny real limits, disability, training needs or unequal opportunity.

source.name: Rick Rubin - Creativity, Taste and the Four Phases (The Diary of a CEO)

pivots.text: Use comparison to identify a technique worth learning, rather than to rank your worth against another person.
pivots.limits: Useful standards and constructive feedback still matter.

source.name: Peter Sage - Four Levels of Consciousness (Lewis Howes)

pivots.text: Distinguish actual feedback and responsibilities from imagined demands to win everyone’s approval.
pivots.limits: Do not assume criticism is imagined or dismiss legitimate feedback.

source.name: Peter Sage - Four Levels of Consciousness (Lewis Howes)

pivots.text: A meaningful process can matter before the final goal is reached. Notice what is worthwhile in today’s work.
pivots.limits: Do not imply distress is a choice or that someone must feel happy.

source.name: Peter Sage - Four Levels of Consciousness (Lewis Howes)

pivots.text: When circumstances change, preserve the purpose while revising the route and the next feasible action.
pivots.limits: Acceptance does not mean accepting harm or abandoning responsibilities.

source.name: Peter Sage - Four Levels of Consciousness (Lewis Howes)

pivots.text: Separate what you can influence from an outcome you cannot guarantee. Choose the next responsible action.
pivots.limits: Releasing outcome control is not giving up agency, planning or protection.

source.name: Chris Williamson — The Lonely Chapter and Evidence Over Self-Belief (Mental Quest)
source.locator: Saved source summary lines 43–47; original media not independently reviewed

pivots.text: A small promise you can realistically keep can provide useful evidence of progress without needing confident feelings first.
pivots.limits: Worth is not earned through productivity, and plans should respect capacity.
